headline: Undeterred by Robertson whiff, Kraken are big-game hunting in trade market
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Kraken are still hunting for help on the trade market despite missing on Robertson, with the goal of adding a scoring winger or a top-four defenseman.

Seattle has a good record so far this season, 9-5-1 for 19 points, but our numbers say the results are running ahead of the play. The Kraken have taken 45 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality, so shot volume and location both count), which means they've been outchanced more often than not. Their goals total sits 9.9 above what those chances would normally produce, and that kind of finishing is hard to hold. Goaltending isn't covering for it either: goals saved above expected is -2.4, so the goalies have been slightly worse than the shots they've faced. At five on five the share is the same 45 percent, so this isn't a special-teams quirk. The power play (0.58 expected goals per game) and penalty kill (0.64 allowed per game) are middling. If Seattle wants to keep this pace, adding offense or defense makes sense, because the underlying play so far this season doesn't match the standings.
